title: When a four-force is not orthogonal to velocity
promptMarkdown: A small body absorbs energy isotropically in its instantaneous rest frame, so it remains at rest in laboratory $S$ while its invariant mass increases at rate $\dot m=\lambda>0$ per unit proper time. Compute $P$, $K=dP/d\tau$, $A$ and $K\cdot U$. Identify exactly why $K=mA$ fails. Explain how the total closed system can still conserve four-momentum, and why the same bookkeeping matters for a fuel-burning rocket.
hintLadder: In the specified rest frame $P^0=mc$ and $dE/dt=\lambda c^2$.
Distinguish conservation for a closed system from the momentum change of one chosen subsystem.
